_readme: THE LANE CONTRACT (DRE-2726). One file, read by everything.
Per lane: the entrance condition, the exit condition, the permitted writers,
and the evidence that justifies occupancy. The guard (scripts/lane_scope.py)
reads its flow from here instead of carrying a copy; the sweep
(scripts/reconcile.py) reads its stall windows from here; the documentation
(docs/lane-contract.md) is RENDERED from here; and the integration harness
asserts the live board against it on every trunk commit.
Every clause carries `enforced_from`: the wave phase at which the harness may
assert it. The harness asserts only clauses whose phase has shipped, and FAILS
when a clause's phase has passed with nothing implementing it. That is what
makes this a schedule that checks itself rather than a description.
JSON, not YAML: scripts/linear_ops.py imports the reader on every product
repo's agent job, where there is no pip install and PyYAML is not guaranteed.
Regenerate the document after any edit:
python3 scripts/lane_contract.py render
Check the live board against it:
python3 scripts/lane_contract.py check --live
Wave 1.5's phases, and how far the wave has actually shipped. `current` is
advanced by the operator prove-cards (DRE-2760..DRE-2768) — and advancing it
is the whole act: every clause at or below it must have an implementation or
the harness fails.

titles.0: the checks that must exist before anything moves
titles.1: Linear set up and the Intake lane visible
titles.2: the lane contract asserted by the harness
titles.3: the gates proven against every card type
titles.4: the agents changed before they touch a card
titles.5: cards flow through the new front door
titles.6: the old structure archived, and the wave closed

why: The transition a card makes leaving the planning segment — where the second
critic writes its verdict. Layer 1 of the guard polices the lanes downstream
of it and nothing upstream, because upstream no verdict can exist yet.
Named after the transition, never after a description of the lanes on one
side of it: a description drifts and takes the guard's scope with it.

_readme: Retired board names, accepted on INPUT so a board mid-rename still resolves
to the right lane. An alias is not a lane and is never written out by the
contract; scripts/linear_ops.py inverts this map for the one write path that
still needs the old name. Delete an entry once no board carries it — this is
the ONE place the retired name survives, and both directions read it here.
Each entry carries the shim marker DRE-2722's sweep looks for, so the
exemption is a declared intent on the line itself and not a path allow-list.
The console's own state vocabulary, which must not diverge from the board.
It lives in another repository, so the harness locates the module by name in
that repo's tree and reads the named symbol. When it cannot reach it, the
clause reports UNEVALUATED — never a pass — and becomes a hard failure from
the phase named on the rule.
Every actor permitted to move a card, and where it lives. A lane names
writers by key; the harness checks the key resolves here and that a writer
with a path still exists in this checkout — a lane whose writer was deleted
is a lane nothing can legally move a card out of.

relay.what: the dispatch Lambda — creates a card's first lane from an inbound event
relay.note: lives in agent-bureau (cloud/relay); no path to check from here

operator.what: a human, working in Linear or running a script by hand

plan.yml.what: the planner — writes an epic's children and moves the epic for approval

agent-task.yml.what: the build run — takes a card from Todo and reports where it landed

agent-fix.yml.what: the fix run — REQUEST_CHANGES or a merge conflict

qa-review.yml.what: the adversarial critic — writes the verdict the gate reads

merge-gate.yml.what: the gate — merges on CI green plus a bound APPROVE

linear-sync.yml.what: the merge seam — closes the card off GitHub's merge event

reconcile.py.what: the ~15-minute sweep — promotion, staleness nudges, unsticking

linear_ops.py.what: the guarded write layer every other writer goes through

mid_epic.py.what: mid-epic discovery — files a sibling into an approved epic

dead_run.py.what: the dead-run cap — parks a card that keeps dying

groomer.py.what: the groomer — moves ONE approved batch out of Intake, in order

critic_score.py.what: the critic's audit — moves a card the critic could not classify, with the reason on it

guard.what: the lane guard — returns a card whose occupancy is unjustified
guard.note: DRE-2725, built in agent-bureau; reads its scope from lane_scope.py

rules.text: No state exists in Linear that the contract does not name.
rules.why: A leftover design-review state sat on the board with one card ever and zero code references, and nobody noticed for four months (DRE-2726 retired it; DRE-2818 deleted the last entry naming it).

rules.text: No lane is named that does not exist in Linear.
rules.why: The other half of the same pair: a contract that names a lane the board dropped is a contract nothing can satisfy.

rules.text: A retiring lane holds no cards.
rules.why: A lane the pipeline no longer writes to is a lane nothing will move a card out of. An occupied one is a stranded card.
rules.pending: Phase 3 is when the wave asserts it. Nothing is retiring today (DRE-2818 deleted the last two entries once Linear archived their states), so the clause is vacuously satisfied and skipped; it earns its keep on the NEXT retirement, where the sweep's drain (reconcile.drain_retiring_lanes) empties the lane and this is what proves the drain finished

rules.text: A retiring entry whose Linear state is already gone is deleted from this file.
rules.why: A retirement that never finishes is drift too. Once the board catches up, the entry is the last copy of a lane that no longer exists.

rules.text: Every lane the pipeline knows appears in the console's state lists, and the console names no state the contract does not carry.
rules.why: The console's vocabulary carried Proposed and HOLD, neither of which is a Linear state, and it renders an Intake column that can never fill.

rules.text: The pipeline's own scripts and workflows name no state the contract does not carry.
rules.why: A workflow that advances a card into an archived state fails its Linear call at 2am, on a card nobody is watching.

rules.text: Every transition observed was made by a writer the destination lane permits.
rules.why: A lane's writer list is only a contract if something reads the transition log against it.
rules.pending: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records

rules.text: Every transition observed carried the evidence the destination lane requires.
rules.why: The evidence clause is the one that makes occupancy justifiable rather than assumed.
rules.pending: the routing verdict exists and is readable (DRE-2724); still needed is the plan artifact gate (DRE-2720) and a writer that stamps every card at planning exit (DRE-2721)

entrance.text: Every writer that creates work writes here first — the relay, the planner, a mid-epic discovery, a human. There is no other valid first lane.
entrance.pending: DRE-2680 points every writer at Intake

exit.text: A classification exists: one-off, epic, or wave.
exit.pending: DRE-2719 makes Planning decide the classification

writers.text: Anything that creates a card, and nothing that moves one onward.

evidence.text: The card exists and carries no classification yet.

lanes.name: Planning
lanes.stale_why: what a Planning card owes is a classification, and producing one is a planner run — plan.yml's job alone is capped at 45 minutes, two planner passes and two critic rounds (DRE-2736, DRE-2721)

entrance.text: The card has been classified as needing a plan.

exit.text: A plan artifact exists. No artifact, no exit.
exit.pending: DRE-2720 writes the artifact; the gate that refuses exit without one is Phase 5

writers.text: The planner, the sweep that re-triggers it, a build run handing back a card that turned out to be an epic, the groomer draining a batch the CEO approved, the critic's audit moving a card it could not classify, and a human.

evidence.text: The plan artifact on the card: business case, KPIs as data, risk, outcome.

entrance.text: A plan is waiting on the CEO, an agent has escalated a question only the CEO can answer, or the post-approval critic sent an approved plan back with a stated reason (DRE-2721).
entrance.pending: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records — the three entrances exist, nothing yet reads a card's arrival against them

exit.text: The CEO answers: an approved plan activates — and its children promote only once the post-approval critic has read it (DRE-2721) — an answered escalation returns to Todo, a rejected one goes to Backlog.
exit.pending: needs the transition history the Phase-5 front door records

writers.text: The planner, the two agent runs that escalate, and a human.

evidence.text: A plan artifact, an escalation comment written in business terms — never code, never a diff — or a `plan-critic:` marker recording the round that sent the plan back (DRE-2721).
evidence.pending: needs routing verdicts (DRE-2724) writing on every card before arrival can be judged against the evidence

entrance.text: It carries a routing verdict — one of the five in config/routing-verdicts.json, machine-readable on the card.
entrance.pending: the vocabulary exists (DRE-2724); what is still missing is a writer that puts a verdict on EVERY card at planning exit — DRE-2721's second critic

exit.text: The verdict's destination is reached. The sweep promotes a FLEET card to Todo once the dependency gate clears and the WIP cap has room; a human moves a WORKBENCH or OPERATOR card to Todo and works it there; a PARKED card does not leave, and is never reported as stalled.
exit.pending: the sweep already refuses to promote a non-FLEET card (DRE-2724); asserting the transitions needs the history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The planner and mid-epic discovery create here; the sweep and the dead-run cap park here.

evidence.text: A routing verdict comment; and, for a child of an epic, an epic that has passed Planning exit.
evidence.pending: the marker exists and the sweep reads it (DRE-2724); asserting that every Backlog card carries one needs the writer at planning exit (DRE-2721)

lanes.name: Todo
lanes.stale_why: a Todo card with no dispatched run is a card nothing is coming for

entrance.text: Its verdict names who builds it here: FLEET for a dispatched agent run, WORKBENCH or OPERATOR for a person — marked `hand-built`, which is what already stops the sweep dispatching a competing run or reporting the card as stranded.
entrance.pending: the sweep promotes only a FLEET card (DRE-2724); asserting occupancy needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: A dispatched run posts its start receipt and the card moves to In Progress — or, on a hand-built card, the person working it opens the pull request.
exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The sweep promotes into it; the build run takes cards out of it.

evidence.text: A verdict whose destination is this lane, no unmet blocking relation, and — for a FLEET card — room under the WIP cap.
evidence.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

lanes.name: In Progress
lanes.stale_why: silent agent deaths requeue from here; 60 minutes is one build's honest ceiling

entrance.text: A dispatched agent run exists for this card.
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: A pull request exists on the card's own branch — or the run died and the card is requeued.
exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The build run, the fix run, and the sweep that requeues a dead one.

evidence.text: The run's start receipt on the card, and a live or completed run behind it.
evidence.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

lanes.name: In Review
lanes.stale_why: the folded lane keeps the longer of the two windows the pair had (120 and 60) — a shorter one re-dispatches reviews that are simply still running
lanes.note: Folded from the two review lanes DRE-2726 retired (DRE-2818 deleted their entries once Linear archived the states). Both meant 'a pull request is open and being checked'; the sweep now keys off the evidence — a verdict bound to the head — rather than off which of two lanes the card sat in.

entrance.text: A pull request is open on the card's branch and is being checked: by the critic, by the verifier, or by the merge gate.
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: GitHub merges the pull request and linear-sync writes Done — or the pull request is gone and the card is requeued under the dead-run cap.
exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The build run puts cards here; the critic, the gate, the fix run and the sweep move them on.

evidence.text: An open pull request; and, once the critic has run, a verdict bound to the head sha.
evidence.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

entrance.text: GitHub merged the card's pull request. The merge event, never an agent's claim.
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.text: None. Done is terminal, and the guarded write layer refuses to un-complete a card that reached it.
exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: The merge seam, the sweep's merged-PR backstop, and a human closing an operator card.

evidence.text: The merge commit on the card's own branch.
evidence.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

lanes.name: Triage
lanes.off_flow_reason: the guard's own destination for a card returned three times — policing it would bounce the sink straight back to Intake and loop

entrance.text: The card itself is malformed and cannot proceed as written: an unroutable repo label, an archived repo, a card the readiness guard has returned three times.
entrance.pending: DRE-2723 defines what may be parked here

exit.text: Somebody fixes the card, and it re-enters at Intake. Triage is not a decision queue — a card waiting on the CEO belongs in Green Light.

writers.text: Whatever found the defect: the relay, the sweep, either agent run, or a human.

evidence.text: The defect, named on the card by whatever bounced it.

lanes.name: Canceled
lanes.off_flow_reason: terminal and off the path; the card makes no claim to justify

entrance.text: A human decided the work will not be done.
entrance.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

exit.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records

writers.text: A human, only. The pipeline never cancels a card.

evidence.text: A human's decision, on the card.
evidence.pending: needs the transition history Phase 5 records
